question: Should OpenClaw core accept this broad opt-in continuation system now, after the small status-row fix, or should the work be split/narrowed before merge?
rationale: The branch is a substantial new model-facing agent lifecycle capability with config, persistent state, compaction, TaskFlow, and cross-session security implications; code review can find defects, but it cannot decide whether this belongs in core at this scope.

options.title: Sponsor core continuation after repair
options.body: Fix the status-row defect, require clean exact-head validation, and have an owner explicitly accept the new continuation config/state/security contract.

options.title: Split the surface
options.body: Land only a smaller maintainer-owned core seam or RFC slice first, leaving broader tool behavior and cross-session routing for later PRs.

options.title: Decline this core direction
options.body: Close or pause this PR if maintainers do not want model-elected continuation and delegate routing in OpenClaw core right now.

recommendation.title: Sponsor core continuation after repair
recommendation.body: Fix the status-row defect, require clean exact-head validation, and have an owner explicitly accept the new continuation config/state/security contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The sampled current-main history points to this person as the strongest available adjacent owner for status/runtime/config review routing.
